sources_considered.why: The GPT-3 authors directly describe long-passage coherence failures.
Contemporaneous planning intervention relevant to the proposed mechanism, with substantial evaluation limitations.
The detailed schedule places TattleTale in the June 15, 2022 session, establishing availability before the post.
Later GPT-3-based planning and revision comparisons are relevant context, but do not isolate the historical causal claim.

evidence_items.locator: Section 5, opening and following paragraph on text synthesis
evidence_items.explanation: The following paragraph reports semantic repetition, loss of coherence over long passages, contradictions and non-sequiturs. This supports the existence of the symptom, but does not identify Marcus’s proposed causes.

evidence_items.publisher: ICAPS 2022 SPARK Workshop; Nisha Simon and Christian Muise
evidence_items.explanation: TattleTale supplies planner-generated actions to GPT-J-6B and reports better narrative consistency. Its limited evaluation and lack of external factual-grounding tests prevent this from settling the broader causal claim.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Kevin Yang, Yuandong Tian, Nanyun Peng and Dan Klein
evidence_items.explanation: Re3 reports better story coherence from a package of planning, repeated context, reranking and editing around GPT-3-based generation. The experiment postdates the claim and does not isolate the three linguistic factors or external factual grounding.

unresolved_gaps: The studies do not isolate the proposed three-factor explanation from extra prompting, planning, revision or computation.
Improved coherence within fictional stories does not establish improved connection to external reality.
No located study directly tests the full causal claim across generation lengths in the historical models.
